evidence: EventTypeEditorViewModel.swift:289-295 verified in working tree: `guard let value = Double(cleaned), value >= 0 else { return nil }; return Int((value * 100).rounded())`. `priceDollars` (line 75) is a plain var with no didSet; EventTypeEditorView.swift:410-414 is a bare TextField(.decimalPad) with no onChange/maxLength clamp. evidence: WhosFreeViewModel.swift verified: load() computes startOfDay with tzCalendar (:245-249, pinned to the home's tz) at :106-107, then serialises it via SchedulingTime.isoDay (:117-118), which hard-codes formatter.timeZone = UTC (SchedulingTime.swift:88-94, verified earlier). For any positive-offset zone the local-midnight instant falls on the previous UTC day: Asia/Tokyo Aug 6 00:00 JST = Aug 5 15:00Z → from="2026-08-05". Backend parses it as UTC midnight (availabilityService.js — new Date(from).getTime(), verified earlier), so the returned window is [Aug 5 09:00 JST, Aug 6 09:00 JST) for the .day mode. freeHours (:164-181) then extracts only hour-of-day in tz and discards the date, folding yesterday's free slots into today's grid — a member busy all day today but free 2-4 PM yesterday renders Free at 2p. Negative offsets get the right day STRING but a window shifted back by the offset, folding late-yesterday hours in. Same pattern confirmed at findATimeHere (:203-204), FindATimeSetupViewModel.swift:229-230, FindATimeSuggestedViewModel.swift:181-182. Android uses LocalDate.now() (no UTC conversion) per claim.
fix: Use the existing tz-aware BookingsCalendar.isoDay(_:tz:) (BookingsSupport.swift:237-244) — or add a SchedulingTime.isoDay(_:tz:) overload — at all four call sites so the day key is formatted in the same zone the start-of-day was computed in.

evidence: InviteeIntakeFormView.swift:373 verified: `ForEach(Array(viewModel.guests.enumerated()), id: \.offset)` — row identity is the array index of a collection that removeGuest(at:) mutates in place (InviteeIntakeFormViewModel.swift:323-326 guests.remove(at:)). evidence: BusinessKit.swift verified: BizAvatar.tint (:194-197) computes `abs(name.hashValue) % Self.tints.count` while the doc comment at :183 promises a 'stable hash'. Swift's String.hashValue is SipHash with a per-process random seed (since Swift 4.2), so the same member maps to a different tint on every cold launch — members are not visually identifiable across sessions and won't match Android's deterministic tinting. Secondary: abs(_:) traps if hashValue happens to be Int.min (theoretical but free to fix).
fix: Hash deterministically over the member id (e.g. FNV-1a over id.utf8 or utf8.reduce with &* &+) and index with .magnitude % tints.count; prefer id over display name so renames keep the color.

evidence: TeamBookingAvailabilityViewModel.swift verified: weekWindow() (:224-232) builds window.days from utcCalendar().startOfDay + ymd (:213-222), i.e. UTC day keys (the :210 comment even says 'YYYY-MM-DD (UTC)'). coverage() (:238-241) derives coveredDays from `String(($0.startLocal ?? $0.start).prefix(10))` and intersects against window.days; startLocal is confirmed tz-LOCAL — SchedulingCommonDTOs.swift:22-23 ('Local ISO rendered in the requested tz') and backend availabilityService.js:562 `DateTime.fromMillis(s.startMs, { zone: vtz }).toISO()`. distinctDayCount (:234-236) mixes the same conventions for each row's bookable flag. In America/Los_Angeles after 5 PM local, UTC is already the next day: window.days = [D+1 … D+7] while local slot keys span [D … D+6], so the final window day can never be covered → spurious 'no coverage — add hours' warning on a fully-configured team.
fix: Build the window in the requested tz (calendar pinned to the VM's tz) so window.days and startLocal prefixes share one zone; when startLocal is absent convert start into tz before taking the prefix.
